study_type_evidence.quote: Thirty U-87 MG tumor-bearing mice (five mice per group) received an intravenous injection of about 1.85 MBq and 0.25 μg of 111In-DOTA-EB-cRGDfK
In vitro stability of 111In-DOTA-EB-cRGDfK was evaluated by incubation with normal saline (in 1:1 vol ratio) or rat plasma (in 1:19 vol ratio)
U-87 MG cells were seeded into 24-well plates at a density of 1 × 105 cells per well and incubated overnight.

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: female non-obese diabetic, severe combined immunodeficiency (NOD/SCID), 6 weeks old, bearing subcutaneous U-87 MG xenografts
in_vivo_species.quote: Female non-obese diabetic, severe combined immunodeficiency (NOD/SCID) mice were obtained from BioLASCO Taiwan Co., Ltd. The 6-week-old mice were housed

ex_vivo_detail: Radiochemical stability of 111In-DOTA-EB-cRGDfK was tested by incubation in rat plasma (1:19 v/v) at room temperature for up to 96 h, assayed by iTLC. The paper calls this 'in vitro stability', but per protocol a plasma incubation is classified ex vivo; the plasma is of rat origin. Normal saline incubation run in parallel is in vitro.
in_vitro_detail: Competitive binding assay in cultured U-87 MG human glioblastoma cells with 10 nM 111In-DOTA-EB-cRGDfK against 0.01-5000 nM unlabelled DOTA-EB-cRGDfK or DOTA-cRGDfK; incubation of the radiotracer in normal saline for stability.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Cumulative urinary and fecal excretion of 111In-DOTA-EB-cRGDfK after the intravenous administration. Each point represents the mean ± SD for five animals.
concentration_time_figure.note: No figure plots blood/plasma concentration against time. Blood radioactivity was sampled at 0.083, 0.5, 2, 4, 24, 48, 72, 96 and 168 h but is summarised only as NCA parameters in Table 3. Figure 4 plots cumulative excretion (%ID in urine and feces) versus time, which is not a concentration-time curve. Table 2 gives organ %ID/g at five timepoints including blood, but is a table, not a figure.

bioanalytical_method: Gamma counting of 111In radioactivity (PerkinElmer 2480 Automatic Gamma Counter), expressed as % injected dose per gram; parameters fitted by noncompartmental analysis in WinNonlin 7.0
bioanalytical_quote: The radioactivity of blood samples was measured by PerkinElmer 2480 gamma counter and expressed as the percentage injected dose per gram (% ID/g).
notes: Only 111In-DOTA-EB-cRGDfK and 111In-DOTA-cRGDfK had pharmacokinetic parameters determined; 111In-DOTA-EB was imaged and described as having a 'long half-life' but no numeric PK values are given for it. Tmax is not reported for either agent, consistent with intravenous bolus dosing. The reported T1/2λz is explicitly the terminal half-life ('Pharmacokinetic parameters associated with the terminal phase were calculated using the best-fit method to estimate the terminal half-life'), so half_life_phase is 'terminal/beta'. Note the paper reports the dosimetry 'biologic half-time was 17.6 h' in Section 2.7, which is a human-extrapolated dosimetry assumption, not a mouse plasma half-life, and is deliberately not recorded as a PK half-life. The plasma stability assay uses RAT plasma even though the in vivo work is in mice.
